label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
I've been tagged in a lot of comments since yesterday, so I'll say this once, here, properly.

@Kavya and I were in Foundry91 Cohort 4 together. Demo day was March. A few days before it, she sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. I haven't forgotten that, and I won't. So this is not a reply to pick a fight. She's a friend, and she has helped me more than most people in this batch know.

Two engineers from SitterNest joined DabbaDost on 3 November. Her post is about that. Some numbers are already being repeated in the comments, so I want to put the actual facts out.

Here's what happened:

- We posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September. Public, open to anyone.
- The first engineer applied on his own on 19 September. The second came about two weeks later as his referral.
- Nobody from our side DMed anyone on her team.
- The offer was 22% over their current CTC. Not 40%.
- On ESOPs: we do have a pool. It's small, but it's real and it has been on paper since January. We didn't promise anything that doesn't exist.

Now the part that's on me.

I knew where both of them worked from day one. I should have called Kavya before making the offers. Instead I messaged her after the second offer was accepted. That's the wrong order, and I understand why it felt like I went around her. If I were in her place, I'd have been upset too. I'm sorry, Kavya.

I'm not naming either engineer, and I'd request everyone in the comments not to either. They applied for a job. They didn't sign up for this thread.

The bigger point for our batch: there are 11 of us, and we're all hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will happen again, to someone else, maybe to me from the other side. So I'd like to suggest one simple rule for Cohort 4:

If you're interviewing someone who works at another batch company, give that founder a heads up before you make the offer.

It's a heads up, not a request for permission. It costs one phone call and saves exactly this kind of week.

Kavya, coffee or a call is open from my side, this week, whenever you're okay. Happy to come to you.
